These 5 power words change the answer because they change the job ChatGPT thinks it's doing. 1. TRUTHMODE: Honesty instead of compliments. Put it before a prompt when you want the model to push back, name weak logic, and stop glazing. 2. /human: Text with less stiffness. Use it before drafts, captions, emails, and posts when you want output with a more natural rhythm. 3. REDTEAM: Pressure testing. Ask ChatGPT to red team your idea and it will look for flaws, hidden assumptions, missing evidence, and failure points. 4. ELI10: Clarity. It pushes the answer into simple language without making you feel talked down to. 5. FUTUREYOU: Advice with perspective. Ask from the version of you who already handled the problem, and the answer often gets calmer and more useful. What are the best ChatGPT prompt words? How do I make ChatGPT more honest? Follow me and DM me "JEV" on IG/FB only 👇 Jev AI is a specialized model for classification and routing. It outputs probabilities instead of writing a response. ChatGPT and Claude look at information, reason through it, and generate text. Jev looks at the same type of information and makes a small decision fast. One engineer replaced ChatGPT Luna with Jev for a classification task. The engineer reported results 5 to 18 times faster, with greater accuracy. This matters because many AI agent workflows rely on repeated classification and routing decisions. Generating extra tokens adds work when the workflow only needs a label, score, route, or yes/no answer. Jev fits tasks such as sorting inputs into categories, choosing which workflow handles a request, ranking or scoring an item, and detecting spam, risk, intent, urgency, topic, or sentiment. The simple rule: use a general LLM when you need language. Use Jev when you need probabilities for a focused classification or routing decision. What is the Jev AI model? Everything you need to learn AI, in one video This one runs longer than my usual videos because it's the one that matters most. By the end you'll know what every piece is — and exactly how to start today, from zero, with no coding background. PART 1 — LEARN AI. The model is a brilliant mind that has read almost everything and knows nothing about you. The whole world is stuck at chat level. Learning AI for real starts when you give that mind YOUR world: plain files about what you sell, who your customers are, how you talk. That's context. Same model everyone uses — yours knows your customers by name. PART 2 — AUTOMATIONS. Work that fires on its own when something happens. Invoice lands → logged → answered, nobody touched anything. Built on a visual canvas with your real tools, and AI sits inside the flow as the thinking step. Business owners I teach run dozens of these — some save hundreds of hours. And once you can do that, you can describe a tool you wish existed and build it: your ideas turn into products. PART 3 — AI EMPLOYEES. An agent is AI with hands and a goal: plan, do, check, fix, again — until the job is done. An AI employee is an agent that STAYS: memory so corrections stick, skills written once and followed every time, working inside your real accounts, behind guardrails — keys only to its own work, and the risky moves wait for your yes. I run my whole business this way. They work while I sleep; mornings, the finished work is waiting. THREE DOORS for the skills: your own work (hand off the repeating hours), your ideas (products people use), or clients (companies pay real money for people who can wire AI into an operation). None of this needs code. First time in history you build all of it in plain English. The ramp: TODAY write your context files → THIS WEEK first automation → THIS MONTH first agent → THEN your first employee. Each step makes the next one easy. A mind alone is potential.
